verses.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the command of God our Savior and Christ Jesus our hope,
to Timothy, my true child in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
As I urged you when I went to Macedonia, stay in Ephesus and instruct certain people not to teach different doctrines
or get caught up in myths and endless family trees. These things lead to arguments instead of advancing God's work, which happens through faith.
The goal of this instruction is love that comes from a pure heart, a good conscience, and genuine faith.
Some have wandered away from these things and turned to empty talk.
They want to be teachers of the law, but they don't understand what they're saying or what they're so sure about.
We know the law is good when someone uses it properly.

We also know that the law wasn't made for those who do right, but for the lawless and rebellious, the ungodly and sinful, the unholy and irreverent, those who kill their fathers or mothers, murderers,
the sexually immoral, men who have sex with men, slave traders, liars, perjurers, and anyone else who acts against sound teaching.
That teaching agrees with the Good News of the glory of the blessed God, which he entrusted to me.
I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who gave me strength. He considered me faithful and appointed me to serve him,
even though I used to blaspheme, persecute, and act violently. But I received mercy because I acted in ignorance and unbelief.
The grace of our Lord overflowed for me, along with the faith and love found in Christ Jesus.
This saying is trustworthy and deserves full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners—and I'm the worst of them.
But I received mercy for this reason: so that in me, the worst sinner, Christ Jesus could show his complete patience as an example for those who would believe in him and receive eternal life.
To the King of the ages, immortal and invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
Timothy, my child, I'm giving you this instruction in line with the prophecies made about you, so you can fight the good fight,
holding on to faith and a good conscience. Some have rejected these and shipwrecked their faith.
Among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I handed over to Satan so they would learn not to blaspheme.
First of all, I urge that requests, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for everyone,
including kings and all those in authority, so we can live peaceful and quiet lives in all godliness and dignity.
This is good and pleasing to God our Savior,
who wants everyone to be saved and to come to know the truth fully.
There is one God and one mediator between God and humanity: Christ Jesus, himself human,
who gave himself as a ransom for everyone. This was the testimony given at the right time.
For this I was appointed a preacher and an apostle—I am telling the truth in Christ, not lying—a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
So I want men everywhere to pray, lifting holy hands without anger or argument.
In the same way, women should dress modestly and with good judgment, not with elaborate hairstyles, gold, pearls, or expensive clothes,
but with good deeds, as is fitting for women who claim to honor God.
A woman should learn quietly and with full submission.
I don't permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man; she should remain quiet.
Adam was formed first, then Eve.
Adam wasn't deceived, but the woman was deceived and became a transgressor.
But women will be saved through childbearing, if they continue in faith, love, and holiness with good judgment.
This saying is trustworthy: if someone wants to serve as an overseer, they desire a good work.
So an overseer must be above reproach, faithful to one wife, clear-minded, self-controlled, respectable, welcoming to guests, and able to teach.
They must not be a drunkard or violent, but gentle, not argumentative or greedy for money.
They must manage their own household well and have children who respect them.
If someone doesn't know how to manage their own household, how can they care for God's church?
They must not be a recent convert, or they may become conceited and fall into the same judgment as the devil.
They must also have a good reputation with outsiders, so they won't fall into disgrace or the devil's trap.
In the same way, church servants must be dignified, sincere, not drinking too much wine, and not chasing dishonest gain.
They must hold on to the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience.
Let them first be tested; then, if nothing is found against them, let them serve.
In the same way, women must be dignified, not slanderers, clear-minded, and faithful in everything.
Church servants must be faithful to one wife and manage their children and households well.
Those who serve well earn a good standing and great confidence in the faith they have in Christ Jesus.
I'm writing these things to you, though I hope to come to you soon.
If I'm delayed, you'll know how people should conduct themselves in God's household, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.

Without question, the mystery of godliness is great: He was revealed in the flesh, vindicated by the Spirit, seen by angels, preached among the nations, believed on in the world, and taken up in glory.
The Spirit clearly says that in later times some will abandon the faith and follow deceptive spirits and teachings from demons.
These teachings come through hypocritical liars whose consciences have been burned as with a hot iron.
They forbid marriage and demand that people avoid certain foods, even though God created these foods to be received with thanks by those who believe and know the truth.
Everything God created is good, and nothing should be rejected if it is received with thanks,
because it is made holy through God's word and prayer.
If you explain these things to the brothers and sisters, you'll be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of faith and the sound teaching you've followed.
Reject irreverent old wives' tales. Instead, train yourself in godliness.
Physical training has some value, but godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for both this life and the life to come.
This saying is trustworthy and deserves full acceptance.
That's why we work hard and struggle: we've put our hope in the living God, who is the Savior of all people, especially of those who believe.
Teach and command these things.
Don't let anyone look down on you because you're young. Be an example to the believers in what you say and do, in love, faith, and purity.
Until I come, focus on the public reading of Scripture, encouragement, and teaching.
Don't neglect the gift you have, which was given to you through prophecy when the elders laid their hands on you.
Practice these things and give yourself fully to them, so everyone can see your progress.
Pay close attention to your life and your teaching. Keep at it, because by doing so you'll save both yourself and those who hear you.
Don't rebuke an older man harshly. Appeal to him as you would your father. Treat younger men like brothers,
older women like mothers, and younger women like sisters—with complete purity.
Give proper care to widows who truly have no one.
If a widow has children or grandchildren, they should first learn to care for their own family and repay their parents. This pleases God.
A widow who truly has no one has placed her hope in God and keeps praying day and night.
But a widow who lives only for pleasure is dead even while she lives.
Teach these things too, so no one can blame them.
Anyone who doesn't provide for their relatives, especially their own household, has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
A widow may be added to the list only if she is at least sixty, has been faithful to one husband,
and is known for good works: raising children, welcoming strangers, washing the feet of God's people, helping those in trouble, and devoting herself to every kind of good work.
Don't put younger widows on the list. When their desires pull them away from Christ, they want to marry,
and they come under judgment for breaking their earlier commitment.
They also learn to be idle, going from house to house. They become not only idle but gossips and busybodies, talking about things they shouldn't.
So I want younger widows to marry, have children, manage their households, and give the enemy no opportunity to criticize.
Some have already turned away to follow Satan.
If a believing woman has widows in her family, she should support them herself so the church won't be burdened and can help widows who truly have no one.
Let the elders who lead well receive double honor, especially those who work hard at preaching and teaching.
Scripture says, ‘Don't muzzle an ox while it's threshing grain,’ and ‘A worker deserves their pay.’
Don't accept an accusation against an elder unless there are two or three witnesses.
Correct those who persist in sin in front of everyone, so the rest will take it seriously.
I charge you before God, Christ Jesus, and the chosen angels: follow these instructions without bias or favoritism.
Don't be too quick to appoint anyone as an elder, and don't share in other people's sins. Keep yourself pure.
Don't drink only water. Take a little wine for your stomach and your frequent illnesses.
The sins of some people are obvious and go ahead of them to judgment. The sins of others show up later.
In the same way, good works are obvious, and even those that aren't obvious can't stay hidden.
Those who are enslaved should consider their masters worthy of full respect, so God's name and our teaching won't be slandered.

If their masters are believers, they must not disrespect them because they're brothers and sisters. Instead, they should serve them even better, because those who benefit from their work are believers and beloved. Teach and urge these things.
If anyone teaches something different and won't agree with the sound teaching of our Lord Jesus Christ and the godly instruction,
they are conceited and understand nothing. They have an unhealthy craving for arguments and word battles, which produce envy, conflict, insults, evil suspicions,
and constant friction among people whose minds are corrupt and who have lost the truth. They think godliness is a way to make money. Stay away from such people.
Godliness with contentment is great gain.
We brought nothing into the world, and we can't take anything out of it.
So if we have food and clothing, we'll be content with that.
Those who are determined to get rich fall into temptation and a trap, and into many foolish and harmful desires that drag people down into ruin and destruction.
The love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some, craving it, have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many pains.
But you, man of God, run from these things. Pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, and gentleness.
Fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of eternal life, which you were called to and confessed when you made your good confession before many witnesses.
I charge you before God, who gives life to everything, and Christ Jesus, who made his good confession before Pontius Pilate:
keep this command without stain or blame until our Lord Jesus Christ appears.
At the right time, God will bring about his appearing—God, the blessed and only Ruler, the King of kings and Lord of lords.
He alone is immortal and lives in unapproachable light. No one has seen him or can see him. To him be honor and eternal power. Amen.
Tell those who are rich in this present age not to be arrogant or put their hope in wealth, which is uncertain, but in God, who richly gives us everything to enjoy.
Tell them to do good, to be rich in good works, and to be generous and ready to share.
By doing this, they'll store up treasure for themselves as a firm foundation for the future, so they can take hold of the life that is truly life.
Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you. Turn away from pointless chatter and the opposing arguments of what is falsely called knowledge.
Some have claimed this knowledge and wandered away from the faith. Grace be with you. Amen.
